summary: Dashboards, reports, charts, sharing and tools as SwiftUI screens.

src/charts/BarList.jsx.note: A Grid of label (136, or 200 for NSIDs set a step smaller), bar (at least 96, or 60) and value, at most 640 wide; each row read as its label and its value, its title (the web's tooltip) the hint; in high contrast the track's edge in --line-soft (theme.css). The web's label may be markup; here a row says whether its label is an NSID (`code`).

src/charts/ChartTable.jsx.note: ChartTable and ShowAsTable: the line under a chart (Show as table as a link action, then the chart's other actions, each 44 points tall with no gap between wrapped lines, as controls.css's touch rules have them; a phone's ⋯ at the line's end), and the buckets newest first in a table at the column's leading edge, as wide as its columns need and at least min(100%, 28rem), at most 320 points and scrolling inside under a head that stays put (the kit's TableScroll over two DataTables, head and rows, each holding every cell, so their columns agree), sideways in its own box when it must, with the trend's column named as the legend names it and each row's head in --ink-2.

src/charts/Heatmap.jsx.note: A Grid of the day labels and the cells on the --heat ramp (ChartFormat.heatSteps), empty cells outlined and the best ringed, every other shaded cell edged in --line-soft in high contrast (theme.css), the hours under them over their spans, and the legend; the summary is the grid's VoiceOver label, each cell's title its tooltip (.help).

src/charts/SeriesChart.jsx.note: In Swift Charts over bucket indices (equal slots): bars (at most 24 wide, a 2-point gap, 90% with the pressed one whole) or a line over the wash with its last dot; the trend (broken at gaps) and its legend; the second line, dashed, or stacked with its wash; the ghost's dashed reach past the last bucket with its open dot and words (drawn through the chart's proxy); the marks' rules and diamonds, and the newest five listed under the chart; the rules with their numbers (fmtTick) and the dates under the first, middle and last bucket (axisStops), the middle one stepping aside when it would run into an end one (the web's 6.6-a-character estimate and 12 clear); a press is the hover (chartXSelection), with the crosshair, the markers and the readout on its own ground (the second series' value strong, the trend's plain); one accessibility element (children ignored, as Heatmap is) labelled with the web's aria label, its peak the web's dataMax (the trend's top and the ghost's reach with the series), as the web's single <svg role="img"> is, with Show as table the way to the values. Swift Charts lays out the plot's margins and the rules' numbers itself (on the leading axis rather than on each rule at the column's edge), and a bar's foot is rounded as well as its top.

src/charts/Sparkline.jsx.note: The web's 100 by 30 box stretched to the width given, 32 tall (or the height asked for: a figure card's 40), the line 1.5 over the wash, gaps left out; hidden from VoiceOver.

src/dashboards/DashboardPage.jsx.note: The header (the name with its ⋯: Rename, Duplicate, New dashboard, Reset or Clear with its toast, Delete with its dialog; the period's line; Customize and the period picker, the picker first and Customize at the row's end on a phone; Done), the twelve-column grid with dashboards.css's narrowing (CardGrid), the cards under their titles (a list's on a rule in ink; a chart's modes under the title in a card 440 wide or less; OwnLine before the count line, each part with the web's title as its hint) with Post this chart (PostChartButton) and the way to the full report, the empty state, and ?edit=1, which leaves the address once read. Customize is the web's phone and keyboard path at every width: each card a line to move up or down, with its name, its figure's number or how many rows it shows, and a chevron; pressing the name opens it (one at a time) to its size on a wide screen under its caption, Settings and Remove, with toasts. The library is a dialog: the count of reports and how many are on this dashboard, the search and the kinds held over the list, which scrolls under them on a rule in ink, each report with its glyph, name, Figure, description, On this dashboard (×n) and Add. The card settings dialog (title, focused; period, kind of engagement and rows as fields; Use the defaults; Cancel and Save in its foot) opens from a card's line. Rename keeps the dialog open for an empty name. Not yet, and why: dragging cards and reports; SwiftUI's draggable and dropDestination give no place between two cards of a custom twelve-column layout to drop on, and List's onMove, the system's long-press reorder, can't hold the grid; the up and down controls are the whole web keyboard path, and VoiceOver's. Nor the wide screen's grid of chosen cards with their floating tools, or the library beside the grid: every width customizes as the web's phone does. The library's search is the web's: a plain lower-cased substring of the name or of the description, each on its own, nothing folded (Catalog.libraryMatches in VirgaInsights, held by LibrarySearchBehaviourTests).
